main_body: A hospital bed seen from above: a headboard with vertical bars at the top, a white pillow and sheet slab, and a blue blanket stripe
top_band: Light grey rim at rows 11-12 (about 2 rows), then a barred headboard face at rows 13-20. The white mattress slab fills rows 22-43 and reads as a flat top-down surface.
evidence: The main body is the mattress, a long white slab with a pillow and a blue blanket stripe, drawn as a plan view. The only front face is a 2-3 row grey edge and dark strip at rows 44-47, which is too thin to read as a south face. The headboard bars are a vertical face with only a 1-2 row cap. No top band, front-edge line, eave shadow or inset front is drawn, so this matches the top-down slab failure in the guide.

style.evidence: The white sheet and pillow are large, nearly flat areas with only one or two shade steps and no texture or grain. The blue blanket is a simple 3-band block. The outline is a uniform dark blue-grey line down both sides, close to neutral. Next to the stall and well references, which have tile scallops, wood grain and stone shading, the tiles hold far fewer colours.
